acceptance.given: A destructive operation is defined or requested.

oracle.expected: The operation documentation or request contains recovery information or an explicit irreversibility disclosure.
forbidden: Neither recovery information nor an irreversibility disclosure is present.
oracle.observable: Destructive-operation documentation or request content includes a recovery or irreversibility disclosure.

acceptance.then: The operation's recovery or irreversibility status is disclosed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a destructive-operation case omitting both recovery information and an irreversibility disclosure; assert the disclosure check fails.

affected_subjects: Destructive operation recovery or irreversibility disclosure
slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate that every destructive operation discloses recovery information or irreversibility.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Reverting restores prior package-validation behavior; no data migration is required.

slice_hint.state_transition: Destructive operation changes from undisclosed to recovery-or-irreversibility disclosed.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator rejects any destructive operation lacking both disclosure forms.

acceptance.given: A destructive-operation request has confirmation derived solely from untrusted input and no trusted authorization source.

oracle.expected: The operation reports failure and does not proceed.
forbidden: The operation succeeds using solely untrusted confirmation.
Untrusted confirmation is accepted as sufficient authorization.
oracle.observable: The authorization result is a failure attributable to the untrusted-only confirmation source.

acceptance.then: The operation fails without initiating the destructive effect.
acceptance.when: The authorization path is invoked with only untrusted confirmation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the untrusted-confirmation case; runtime observation must fail if the operation succeeds or performs the destructive action.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Deny destructive operations confirmed solely by untrusted input.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Authorization behavior can be reverted without schema or state migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Untrusted-only request changes to failed and non-executing.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted test observes failure and no destructive effect.

acceptance.given: A destructive-operation request lacks an affected-scope declaration.

oracle.expected: The operation reports failure before any destructive effect starts.
forbidden: The operation succeeds with missing scope.
A destructive effect starts despite missing scope.
oracle.observable: The result is a failure caused by the missing affected scope.

acceptance.then: The operation fails without initiating the destructive effect.
acceptance.when: The destructive-operation path is invoked without an affected-scope declaration.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the missing-scope case; runtime observation must fail if the operation succeeds or starts a destructive effect.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Deny destructive-operation requests that omit affected scope.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Scope-validation behavior can be reverted without migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Missing-scope request changes to failed and non-executing.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted test observes failure and no destructive effect.

acceptance.given: A destructive-operation request includes a bypass flag as the basis for proceeding.

oracle.expected: The operation reports failure and required confirmation or authorization controls remain enforced.
forbidden: The bypass flag causes successful execution.
The bypass flag circumvents confirmation or authorization.
oracle.observable: The result is a failure attributable to the bypass flag and no control is bypassed.

acceptance.then: The operation fails without initiating the destructive effect.
acceptance.when: The authorization path is invoked with a bypass flag.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the bypass-flag case; runtime observation must fail if the operation proceeds or bypasses authorization controls.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Deny destructive-operation requests that attempt to proceed with a bypass flag.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Bypass enforcement can be reverted without migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Bypass-flag request changes to failed and non-executing.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted test observes failure and confirms authorization was not bypassed.
